llm.summary: The skill's files, templates, and runtime instructions are internally consistent with a persona/workspace manager that operates on ~/workspace and uses only standard Unix tools; no unexplained credential or network requirements are present, but you should review the included scripts before granting execution rights.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (AI Persona OS) matches the supplied artifacts: many templates (SOUL.md, MEMORY.md, HEARTBEAT, etc.), helper scripts, and workflows for building an agent workspace. Required binaries (bash, sed, find, wc, stat, grep) are reasonable for text-file setup and inspection. The presence of cron templates and openclaw CLI mentions are explained as optional features. Overall the requested tools and files align with the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly tells the agent to operate via exec and to confine file operations to ~/workspace; it requires exact verbatim menu text and an agent-driven, zero-terminal setup flow. That is coherent with a hands-off user experience but places emphasis on automated exec calls. The SKILL.md repeatedly prohibits modifying files outside ~/workspace and requires user approval before first-run setup and for opt-in cron/gateway actions. These scope guards are good, but because the agent is instructed to run shell commands (scripts/...), you should review the actual script contents to confirm they truly only read/write workspace files and have no hidden external calls or broader filesystem access.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no network install spec — the skill is instruction- and asset-based with included scripts and templates. That lowers supply-chain risk compared to arbitrary downloads. However, the package includes many shell scripts (including a large setup-wizard and security-audit script) that the agent can execute via exec; that means code on disk may run in your environment, so inspect those files before approving execution.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials. External integrations (cron jobs, gateway/channel operations, sending messages) are clearly marked as opt-in and would require credentials when enabled, but those creds are not requested by default. The included TEAM/TOOLS templates mention platform tokens and env var patterns only as guidance; this is proportionate to a workspace/agent manager.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (not force-included) and model invocation is allowed (the platform default). The potential risk vector is the agent's repeated instruction to use exec for setup and to run scripts — the skill depends on explicit user approval before setup, but you should confirm the platform will present and log those exec approval prompts. No skill-level setting gives permanent elevation, and the skill does not request system-wide config writes by default.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears coherent for building a local agent workspace, but before installing or approving any exec runs: 1) open and review the largest scripts (scripts/setup-wizard.sh, scripts/security-audit.sh, scripts/status.sh) to confirm they only operate on ~/workspace and do not call external URLs or read sensitive system files; 2) verify your OpenClaw platform prompts/consents for exec actions are enabled so the agent cannot run commands silently; 3) keep cron and gateway changes disabled unless you explicitly opt in and have reviewed what those commands will do and what credentials they will require; 4) consider testing in a disposable/sandbox environment first; and 5) if you need higher assurance, paste the contents of the key scripts here or in a safe review channel for a line-by-line check.
